title: Ragtime versus improvisation
summary: He says ragtime did not allow improvisation and was corny to him, while gospel and spirituals were the root.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Now I want to go back for just a moment to something you said about Rag Time. So Rag Time did not provide for improvisation the way that jazz does?

No, no. Absolutely not. It was sort of a, I don't know, the 'Twelfth Street Rag,' that's a rag. You could improvise actually on it now, but the people want to hear that, da, da, da, da, (IMITATES RAG)................ which is, doesn't fit in with my musical taste (I assure you) as jazz. But we used to call it on the corny line. It isn't there.
Whereas to me, the gospel and spirituals, that was it. Basically it.
